rupturesRcpp

rupturesRcpp detects change-points in multivariate time series. It implements the cost functions and search methods of the Python library ruptures in C++, behind an R6 interface, and also accepts cost functions written in R. It was created during Google Summer of Code 2025 for the R Project for Statistical Computing.

install.packages("rupturesRcpp",
                 repos = c("https://edelweiss611428.r-universe.dev",
                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

This installs the development version that the guide documents; see Installation for the CRAN release.

Guide

Getting started

  1. Introduction: what change-point detection is, and the three choices behind every detection.
  2. Overview: one complete detection, from data to plot.
  3. Installation: the development version and the CRAN release.

User guide

  1. Cost functions: the built-in costs, their options, and costs written in R.
  2. Segmentation methods: binSeg, Window, PELT and Dynp, their methods and active bindings.
  3. Model selection: choosing the number of change-points with the elbow method or Dynp.
  4. Segment costs and parameters: $segments() and costFactory.

Examples

  1. Examples and case studies: worked examples on simulated data. Case studies on real data are to be added.

Every class is documented in the function reference, and in R, e.g. ?PELT.

References

  • Truong, C., Oudre, L. and Vayatis, N. (2020). Selective review of offline change point detection methods. Signal Processing, 167, 107299.
  • Killick, R., Fearnhead, P. and Eckley, I. A. (2012). Optimal detection of changepoints with a linear computational cost. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 107(500), 1590–1598.
  • Hocking, T. D. (2024). Finite sample complexity analysis of binary segmentation. arXiv:2410.08654.
